<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="ChristusRex" />{{rh/1|{{larger|{{sc|THE PREFACE}}}}}}</noinclude>{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Hovv the laietie of tho{{ls}}e daies did read them, vvith what humilitie and religion, and enformation of life and maners.}}and p{{ls}}almes either in knowen or vnknowen languages, as they heard them in the holy Church, though they could neither reade nor know the {{ls}}en{{ls}}e, meaning, and my{{ls}}teries of the {{ls}}ame. Such holy per{{ls}}ons of both {{ls}}exes, to whom S. Hierom in diuers Epi{{ls}}tles to them, commendeth the reading and meditation of holy Scriptures, were diligent to {{ls}}earche all the godly hi{{ls}}tories & imitable examples of cha{{ls}}titie, humilitie, obedience, clemencie, pouertie, penance, renoūcing the world: they noted {{ls}}pecially the places that did breede the hatred of {{ls}}inne, feare of Gods iudgement, delight in {{ls}}piritual cogitations: they referred them {{ls}}elues in all hard places, to the iudgement of the auncient fathers and their mai{{ls}}ters in religion, neuer pre{{ls}}uming to contend, controule, teach or talke of their owne {{ls}}en{{ls}}e and phanta{{ls}}ie, in deepe que{{ls}}tions of diuinitie. Then the Virgins, did meditate vpon the places and examples of cha{{ls}}titie, mode{{ls}}tie and demurene{{ls}}{{ls}}e: the maried, on coniugal faith and continencie: the parents, how to bring vp their children in faith and feare of God: the Prince, how to rule: the {{ls}}ubiect, how to obey: the Prie{{ls}}t, how to teach: the people, how to learne.

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The fathers {{ls}}harply reprehend as an abu{{ls}}e, that al indifferently {{ls}}hould reade, expound, and talke of the Scriptures.}}Then the {{ls}}choler taught not his mai{{ls}}ter, the {{ls}}heepe controuled not the Pa{{ls}}tor, the yong {{ls}}tudent {{ls}}et not the Doctor to {{ls}}choole, not reproued their fathers of error & ignorance. Or if any were in tho{{ls}}e better daies (as in al times of here{{ls}}ie {{ls}}uch mu{{ls}}t needes be) that had itching eares, tikling tonges and wittes, curious and contentious di{{ls}}puters, hearers, and talkers rather then doers of Gods word: {{ls}}uch the Fathers did euer {{ls}}harply reprehend, counting them vnworthy and vnprofitable readers of the holy Scriptures. S. Hierom in his Epi{{ls}}tle to Paulinus, after declaration that no handy craft is {{ls}}o ba{{ls}}e, nor liberall {{ls}}cience {{ls}}o ea{{ls}}y, that can be had without a mai{{ls}}ter (which S. Augu{{ls}}tine al{{ls}}o affirmeth, ''De vtilitate cred. cap. 7.'') nor that men pre{{ls}}ume in any occupation to {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Hiero. ep. 103 c. 6.''}}teach that they neuer learned, Only ({{ls}}aith he) ''the art of Scripture is that vvhich euery man chalengeth: this the chatting old vvife, this the doting old man, this the brabling {{ls}}ophi{{ls}}ter, this on euery hand, men pre{{ls}}ume to teach before they learne it.'' Againe, ''Some vvith poi{{ls}}e of lofty wordes deui{{ls}}e of {{ls}}cripture matters among vvomen: other{{ls}}ome (phy vpon it) learne of vvomen, what to teach men, and le{{ls}}t that be not ynough, by facilitie of tong, or rather audacitie, teach that to others, vvhich they vnder{{ls}}tand neuer a vvhit them {{ls}}elues. to {{ls}}ay nothing of {{ls}}uch as be of my facultie: vvho {{ls}}tepping from {{ls}}ecular learning to holy {{ls}}criptures, and able to tickle the eares of the multitude vvith a {{ls}}mothe tale, thinke all they {{ls}}peake, to be the Law of God.'' This he wrote then, when this maladie of arrogancie and pre{{ls}}umption in diuine matters, vvas nothing {{ls}}o outragious as now it is.

S. Gregorie Nazianzene made an oration {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''In orat. de moderatio. in di{{ls}}puta. {{ls}}eruanda.''}}of the moderation that vvas to be v{{ls}}ed in the{{ls}}e matters: where he {{ls}}aith, that {{ls}}ome in his time thought them {{ls}}elues to haue all the wi{{ls}}edom in the world, when they could once repeat tvvo or three wordes, and them ill couched together, out of Scriptures. but he there diuinely di{{ls}}cour{{ls}}eth of the orders and differences of degrees: how in Chri{{ls}}tes my{{ls}}ticall body, {{ls}}ome are ordeined to learne, {{ls}}ome to teach: that all are not Apo{{ls}}tles, all Doctors, all interpreters, all of tonges and knovvledge, not all learned in Scriptures & diuinitie: that the people went not vp to talke with God in the mountaine, but Moy{{ls}}es, Aaron, & Eleazar: nor they neither, but by the difference of their callings: that they that rebell again{{ls}}t this ordinance, are guilty of the con{{ls}}piracie of Corè & his cōplices: that in Scripture there is both milke for babes, and meate for men, to be di{{ls}}pen{{ls}}ed, not according to euery ones<noinclude>{{continues|greedines}}</noinclude>
